title: Creation Station — Art and Science Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the hands-on art and science projects and what they taught us about God's creation!

questions.question: What does a seed need to grow into a plant?
questions.explanation: God designed seeds to grow when they receive water, soil, and sunlight. These are the things every plant needs to live and grow.

questions.question: What happens to construction paper left in the sun?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is powerful and causes the color on construction paper to fade. Objects placed on the paper block the sunlight and keep those spots dark.

questions.question: What covers most of the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: About 70 percent of Earth's surface is covered with water. God filled the oceans, rivers, and lakes with water that all living things need.

questions.question: What kinds of objects do magnets attract?
questions.explanation: God designed magnetism to work with metals like iron and steel. Magnets do not attract wood, paper, or plastic.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about God and the birds?
questions.explanation: Jesus said to look at the birds because God feeds them, even though they do not plant or harvest. He cares for us even more (Matthew 6:26).

questions.question: What does a rain gauge measure?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge measures how much rain falls in a certain area. It helps us see how much water God sends to the Earth.

questions.question: What happens when you put two north poles of a magnet together?
questions.explanation: When two of the same poles (north-north or south-south) are brought together, they push apart. This is called repelling.

questions.question: Why did God create the water cycle?
options: To keep water moving so living things have what they need
questions.explanation: God designed the water cycle so that water evaporates, forms clouds, and falls as rain. This keeps water moving to provide for all living things on Earth.
